title: Tab Name when connecting via an SSH Tunnel
author: vndnua
body_snippet: If the connection is established via an SSH tunnel, the tab does not display the name specified in that connection's settings, but rather “login@host:~ (login )” as shown in the screenshot. This makes it difficult to navigate between tabs, especially when there are several of them. Is there a way to configure this? I haven't been able to find one. Nightly Buil...

comments.author: robertpopa22
comments.snippet:
Thank you for the screenshot; six tabs all named `admin@...:~ (admin)` made the cause easy to find.

This is a defect, not a setting. A connection opened through an SSH tunnel shares its tab with the hidden PuTTY session that carries the tunnel. That hidden session replaced the tab caption with its own shell title, as a normal SSH tab does. The hidden tunnel session no longer changes the caption, so the tab shows the same caption as the same connection opened without a tunnel. An SSH connection ...

comments.author: vndnua
comments.snippet: Yes, I can confirm that the tab caption now displays the correct information. Thank you.

comments.author: robertpopa22
comments.snippet:
Thank you for testing the nightly the same day and for the screenshot: it shows the connection names back on the tunnelled tabs, which is the part we could not check with your gateway.

Closing as fixed. If a tab name goes wrong again, for example with several tunnelled tabs at once, comment here and it reopens.
